dialog.speaker: A
dialog.text: How's that new chick you've been seeing?

dialog.speaker: B
dialog.text: We've been on like 8 dates and she won't even let me kiss her. I feel like I'm in grade school again.

dialog.speaker: A
dialog.text: That's ridiculous. Why don't you just ditch her if she won't put out after 8 dates?

dialog.speaker: B
dialog.text: I don't know. I like the challenge even though it's causing me so much grief in the process. I'm pretty interested to see how all this is going to pan out. I feel she might be starting to warm up a bit. She's smokin hot too so that also plays into it.

dialog.speaker: A
dialog.text: Do you think she likes you or is she just a gold digger?

dialog.speaker: B
dialog.text: It's hard to tell to be honest. Her family is fairly well off so I don't think she's in it just for the money, but you never know.

vocabulary.definition: This is an expression in spoken English that means something like, "Let's not even talk about this topic because once I start, I've got a really long story about it".
This is a very slang use of the word "like". It means "about" or "around" or "approximately". Not exactly but close. I'm not sure exactly how old he is but he's gotta be like 50 or something.

This is the school that people went to when they were kids. This is usually from "grade 1 to grade 8". Grade 9 to Grade 12 is high school. Grade 1 kids about about 5 years old and Grade 8 kids are around 13.
This is a common expression for the idea of "dumping" or breaking up with someone. She ditched him as soon as she found out he was dating other girls.
If some girl doesn't "put out" it means that she doesn't let anyone sleep with her or do anything sexual with her.

If you want to see how something "pans out" it means you want to see the result or conclusion. You want to wait and see the end of the story. I'm not sure if this business idea is going to work or not but I'm really interested to see how it's going to pan out.
In this sense, if a girl is starting to "warm up" it means she's starting to like you more and more. I think she hated my jokes and personality when we first met, but she's starting to warm up a bit.

If you say that something also "plays into it" it means that it's a factor or a part in the decison. I'm not going to that restaurant only because all the waitresses there are super hot, but obviously that plays into it a bit.

If some girl is a "gold digger" it means that she meets guys just for their money. She dates rich guys and it's as simple as that. Maybe she likes them too, but how much money they have is probably the #1 quality they look for in a man.

If you are "in something for the money" it means that the biggest reason you are doing something is because of how much money you think you will get from it. If you are not in it for the money, it means you have other reasons for doing it. Some NBA basketball players want to win a championship more than anything else. Some players just seem like they are in it for the money and don't really care about winning.
